content:
anna: Heads-up — seeing weird output drift on mixed-precision matmul after yesterday's routing change. Small prompts are fine, long ones diverge.
rajeev: ugh, can you paste a minimal repro? sequence length where it starts?
anna: repro attached inline. fails consistently once seq_len > 384 but was previously > 512. here's a trimmed log:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] kernel_select: chosen=k_v1 fp16_accum
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] kv_cache: pack_layout=packed_v2 scale=0.0032
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] matmul: use_kernel=mixed_fp8_accum_v2
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] OUTPUT_DIFF: checksum_delta=0.0021
```
luis: checksum_delta looks tiny but causes downstream token shifts, right? any quant calibration logs?
anna: yes, calibration table shows a sudden scale jump for activations at layer 6 when batch merges happen during queuing. looks correlated with kernel version flip.
mei: are we sure it's kernel selection and not batching heuristic? we changed batch-merging to favor latency earlier.
anna: I added a deterministic run forcing single-batch (no merge) and the drift disappears.
luis: pinging perf-bot for profiling traces
perf-bot: profiler: trace id 0x7f3a - hot-path: matmul_accum -> quantize_activation -> conv_kv_pack. Avg latency +4.2ms when using mixed_fp8_accum_v2.
rajeev: can someone dump the kernel-selection condition? my suspicion: sequence-length boundary changed and we started picking v2 which uses FP8 activation packing with a smaller accumulator headroom.
anna: here's the simplified selector i found in codebase:
```
if (seq_len <= 384) {
  select(kernel_v1); // wider accumulator
} else {
  select(kernel_v2); // faster, FP8-packed accum
}
```
mei: that matches the new routing table change. v2 assumes activation_scale <= 0.004, but kv_cache pack occasionally rescaled to 0.006 when merging batches.
luis: so scale mismatch + narrower accumulator -> saturation and tiny numeric drift, which cascades during softmax -> token shift. nasty.
anna: repro script attached in thread. steps: 1) warm KV cache with batched requests 2) trigger pack_merge 3) run seq_len 400 prompt -> divergence
rajeev: possible immediate mitigations: force v1 for now or clamp activation_scale during pack to expected range. which is cheaper?
mei: forcing v1 increases tail latency ~3ms but stable. clamping might hide a real calibration bug.
luis: we should do both: temporary route to v1 for affected ranges + add pack-time assert on scale to fail fast in CI.
perf-bot: action item created: PERF-789 add scale-assert + selector guard
anna: I pushed a local branch `hotfix/accum-guard` with a quick patch that forces v1 if activation_scale > 0.0045. test pass locally.
rajeev: can you open a PR? include microbench numbers (p95, p99) and unit that reproduces checksum_delta.
anna: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/accum-guard - includes test and repro harness
mei: long-term: we should make kernel_v2 resilient by expanding accumulator dynamic range or add per-layer calibration that updates when batching patterns change.
luis: also add a per-request tag to avoid mixing calibration data from incompatible packing formats into the global table.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for canary at 2026-03-17T14:00:00Z (canary: eng-runtime-canary)
anna: thanks — will monitor canary logs and push rollback if token divergence appears in traces.
rajeev: also add a small fuzz-run to evals to catch similar scale jumps for different models.
mei: agree. tagging infra teams to watch KV pack metrics (pack_rescale_count)
luis: created dashboard tile `KV pack scale` and alert when >0.1% of requests rescaled
anna: great. if canary looks good i'll queue wider rollout. thx everyone :thumbsup:
